# Revenuecat — Style Reference

> Indigo-dyed ledger paper pinned with a periwinkle pill. Object Sans headlines tracked tight at -0.04em on a #ffffff canvas, ruled with #eaedf6 hairlines, with one #576ddb capsule doing all the asking.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

RevenueCat uses an indigo-steeped developer-commerce language. The canvas is #ffffff Paper Canvas. A #f9f9fb Mist Surface tints the hero band and the illustration tiles. Black does not appear anywhere: all text is #1f1f47 ink (67 elements), and the secondary #3d3d5c (45) and tertiary #6c7693 step down the same violet-gray ramp. The chromatic budget is two saturated hues. Periwinkle #576ddb fills every action pill, and its darker sibling #3d52b8 carries links. Coral #f2545c is reserved for the wordmark and for highlighted numerals. Three frosted tints (#c1c9f6, #f7d4d4, #c1f6e0) appear only as washes on card corners and halos behind icons. Object Sans carries the hierarchy through size and a uniform -0.04em tracking from 28px to 60px. Section heads use weight 500, smaller headings use 400 or 300, and Helvetica Neue Light at 16px and 20px does the reading. Cards are 16px-radius rectangles and actions are 9999px pills, lifted by violet-tinted shadows instead of gray ones. The page reads as a dyed ledger rather than a gray dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page body, department sections, input fill and icon chips (35 backgrounds). This is the neutral stage on which the indigo-tinted neutrals register as tinted. |
| Mist Surface | `#f9f9fb` | `--color-mist-surface` | Hero band, logo strip, feature illustration tiles and secondary button fill (35 backgrounds including a merged near-duplicate). It separates bands with tone alone, so no rule lines are needed. |
| Indigo Ink | `#1f1f47` | `--color-indigo-ink` | Every headline, nav label, input value and card title (67 uses). It replaces black with a dyed navy, and this substitution is the thesis of the system. |
| Slate Body | `#3d3d5c` | `--color-slate-body` | Paragraphs, hero lede, the "Log in" link and stat labels (45 uses). It is the reading color and stays in the violet family so that long copy keeps the brand tint. |
| Pewter Caption | `#6c7693` | `--color-pewter-caption` | Eyebrow labels, micro-captions and muted metadata (6 uses). It is the quietest text tone. Do not use it for body paragraphs, because contrast falls too far. |
| Quartz Border | `#eaedf6` | `--color-quartz-border` | Card outlines, input ring, stat-row dividers and panel edges (11 borders). It is a cool hairline that reads as a crease, not a frame. |
| Lavender Ring | `#8998e6` | `--color-lavender-ring` | Outline of the "Contact sales" secondary pill. It links the secondary button to the primary blue without filling it. Do not use it as a general border color. |
| Periwinkle Signal | `#576ddb` | `--color-periwinkle-signal` | "Start for free" and "Sign up" pill fills, plus stat numerals and icon glyphs (10 uses). It is the single action color, so a page should have one dominant fill of it. |
| Cobalt Link | `#3d52b8` | `--color-cobalt-link` | Card "For … teams >" links, "See the docs >" and secondary button text (20 uses). It is a darker periwinkle, so links stay legible at 14px without competing with the fill. |
| Ember Coral | `#f2545c` | `--color-ember-coral` | The RevenueCat wordmark, the "6000+" statistic highlight and the marketing icon glyph (11 uses). It is rationed brand heat. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |
| Frosted Lilac | `#c1c9f6` | `--color-frosted-lilac` | Gradient wash at the corner of the Engineering and Support cards, plus halos around icon chips. It is a decorative tint only and is never used as a text or solid panel color. |
| Frosted Rose | `#f7d4d4` | `--color-frosted-rose` | The Marketing card wash and the coral icon halo. It pairs with Ember Coral the way Lilac pairs with Periwinkle, which gives each department its own temperature. |
| Frosted Mint | `#c1f6e0` | `--color-frosted-mint` | The Product card wash and the green icon halo. It is the only green in the system and appears as a tint, never as a status fill. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Object Sans — geometric display and UI voice for headlines, nav and buttons · `--font-object-sans`
- **Substitute:** Plus Jakarta Sans at 500, Manrope at 500, DM Sans at 500. Object Sans draws slightly wider and a touch heavier than its nominal number. Match its Light 300 with Plus Jakarta Sans 400 or Manrope 400 rather than 300, which would read hairline-thin.
- **Weights:** 300, 400, 500, 700
- **Sizes:** 14px, 16px, 24px, 28px, 30px, 32px, 40px, 48px, 56px, 60px, 80px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.125, 1.333, 1.375, 1.43, 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** -0.32px at 16px (buttons), -0.48px at 24px, -0.64px at 32px, -1.12px at 28px, -1.2px at 30px, -1.6px at 40px, -1.92px at 48px, -2.24px at 56px, -2.4px at 60px, -3.2px at 80px
- **Role:** Every size from 28px upward is tracked at exactly -0.04em. This is a single rule rather than per-size tuning, and it turns headlines into compact, logo-like blocks. Weight 500 at display sizes is the ceiling for section heads. The 700 weight survives in only 6 elements, so emphasis comes from size and not from boldness. The 14px/400 nav setting (67 uses) is the most-used text style in the system, which makes this the workhorse face as well as the display face.

### Helvetica Neue — light-weight reading face for paragraphs and captions · `--font-helvetica-neue`
- **Substitute:** Inter at 350, Public Sans at 300, Nunito Sans at 300. Helvetica Neue Light renders slightly heavier than Inter 300, so Inter 350 (variable) matches the stroke without going spindly.
- **Weights:** 300, 400, 500
- **Sizes:** 12px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 22px
- **Line height:** 1.25, 1.375, 1.5, 1.56
- **Letter spacing:** -0.12px at 12px, -0.4px at 20px (one variant), 0px elsewhere
- **Role:** Body copy sits at weight 300 (48 uses), which is anti-convention, since most SaaS sites set paragraphs at 400. The light grey-violet text recedes behind the 500-weight headlines. Pairing a geometric display face with a neo-grotesk body face splits the voice: Object Sans speaks, and Helvetica Neue explains. Weight 500 at 18px is reserved for short card titles in the feature tiles.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Helvetica Neue | 400 | 12px | 1.25 | -0.12px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Object Sans | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Helvetica Neue | 300 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Helvetica Neue | 300 | 18px | 1.56 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Helvetica Neue | 300 | 20px | 1.375 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Object Sans | 500 | 24px | 1.375 | -0.48px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Object Sans | 400 | 28px | 1.0 | -1.12px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Object Sans | 500 | 32px | 1.125 | -0.64px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Object Sans | 500 | 56px | 1.125 | -2.24px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Object Sans | 500 | 60px | 1.125 | -2.4px | `--text-display` |

The jump from heading (32px) to heading-lg (56px) is a 1.75 step. The lower steps hover near a Minor Third (1.2) and the top step is far steeper than a Perfect Fourth (1.333). The scale is gentle for UI and abrupt for section statements.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Pull every text color from the indigo ramp: #1f1f47 for headings, #3d3d5c for body and #6c7693 for captions. The dye is the brand before any accent appears.
- Track Object Sans at -0.04em from 28px upward (-1.12px at 28px, -2.24px at 56px, -2.4px at 60px). This compresses the geometric letterforms into dense, wordmark-like blocks.
- Fill primary actions with #576ddb in a 9999px pill at Object Sans 16px/500, using 0 28px padding and 48px height. One action color makes every CTA instantly scannable.
- Set paragraphs in Helvetica Neue 300 at 16px/1.5 in #3d3d5c. The light reading weight lets 500-weight headlines dominate without bold body copy competing.
- Tint every shadow toward violet, for example `0px 6px 16px 0px rgba(61, 75, 143, 0.15)` on floating fields. Lift stays inside the indigo family instead of dropping gray smudges.
- Hold containers at 16px radius and actions at 9999px. Two shapes divide the page cleanly into things you read and things you press.
- Ration #f2545c to the wordmark and at most one highlighted numeral per section. Coral is a seal, and its scarcity is what makes it legible.

### Don't
- Don't reach for a neutral gray such as #333333 (not a system token) for body copy. It drains the indigo dye that defines the system, and #3d3d5c as the reading color is non-negotiable.
- Don't fill a CTA with #f2545c because it is "the brand color". Two competing action hues split the signal that #576ddb was built to carry alone.
- Don't push headlines to weight 700. Object Sans 700 appears in only 6 elements at 24px, and display sizes at 500 with -0.04em tracking already carry all the authority needed.
- Don't use black-based shadows like rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2). On the #f9f9fb canvas a gray halo reads as dirt instead of lift.
- Don't square primary buttons down to 4px. The 4px radius belongs only to nav hit zones, and a 4px CTA reads as a form control rather than an invitation.
- Don't use #c1c9f6, #f7d4d4 or #c1f6e0 as solid panel fills or text colors. They are corner washes and halos, and at full strength they turn the page into a pastel dashboard.
- Never ship 56px headlines at 0px tracking. Object Sans spreads wide at default spacing and loses the compact block silhouette.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- text: #1f1f47 (Indigo Ink)
- body text: #3d3d5c (Slate Body)
- background: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- band surface: #f9f9fb (Mist Surface)
- border: #eaedf6 (Quartz Border)
- link: #3d52b8 (Cobalt Link)
- brand highlight: #f2545c (Ember Coral)
- primary action: #576ddb (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts use #576ddb lines and dots at 2px stroke on a #ffffff plot ruled with #eaedf6 gridlines. Secondary series use #3d52b8 or a #c1c9f6 area tint at 40% opacity, and #f2545c is reserved for a single highlighted value, so no chart ever outshouts the primary CTA.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: a `<button>` with background #576ddb, text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 9999px, height 48px and padding 0 28px. Set the label in Object Sans (fallback Plus Jakarta Sans 500) at 16px, weight 500, line-height 1.0 and letter-spacing -0.32px, with no box-shadow. Build a 36px-tall nav variant with padding 0 18px at 14px/500. Next to it, place a secondary pill with background #f9f9fb, text #3d52b8, a 1px solid #8998e6 border, the same 9999px radius, a 36px height and 0 18px padding at 14px/500.

2. Build the hero section on a full-width #f9f9fb band, centered in a 1280px container with 96px top and bottom padding and two columns. In the left column, set the H1 "Build and grow your app business" in Object Sans 60px, weight 500, line-height 1.125, letter-spacing -2.4px, color #1f1f47. Below it, set a 24px-gap lede in Helvetica Neue 20px/400, line-height 1.375, color #3d3d5c, max-width 580px. Next comes a 32px-gap email capture: a 480×64px #ffffff input with a 1px #eaedf6 border, 9999px radius, 28px left padding and shadow `0px 6px 16px 0px rgba(61, 75, 143, 0.15)`, with a 48px #576ddb pill button inset at the right. Finish the column with a three-stat row: numerals in Object Sans 24px/500 #576ddb and labels in Helvetica Neue 16px/300 #3d3d5c, divided by 1px #eaedf6 vertical rules. In the right column, place overlapping white UI panels with 16px radius, a 1px #eaedf6 border and shadow `5px 5px 20px 0px rgba(71, 92, 133, 0.1), 0px 30px 60px 0px rgba(144, 138, 208, 0.1)`.

3. Build a Department Card about 302px wide: background #ffffff with a linear-gradient wash from #c1c9f6 at 30% opacity in the top-left corner fading to transparent by 60%, a 1px solid #eaedf6 border, 16px radius and 24px padding. At the top, place a 40px #ffffff circle (9999px radius) holding a #576ddb filled glyph, with shadow `0px 6px 20px 0px rgba(230, 233, 248, 0.7), 0px 2px 8px 0px rgba(92, 112, 214, 0.2)`. At a 16px gap, set the title "Engineering" in Object Sans 28px/400, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing -1.12px, #1f1f47. At an 8px gap, set the body in Helvetica Neue 16px/300, line-height 1.5, #3d3d5c. At a 24px gap, add the link "For engineering teams >" in Object Sans 14px/500 #3d52b8. Lay the cards out in a horizontal row with a 32px gap.

4. Build the Navigation Bar: 64px tall, transparent background, position relative, no border or shadow, inside a 1280px container. On the left, place the wordmark in #f2545c, then menu triggers "Why RevenueCat?", "Solutions", "Developers", "Resources" and "Pricing". Set each trigger in Object Sans 14px/400, line-height 1.43, #1f1f47, with padding 0 12px, a 4px radius hover zone at full 64px height and a small chevron after dropdown items. On the right, with a 16px gap, place "Log in" as text in Object Sans 14px/500 #3d3d5c, a "Contact sales" outline pill (#f9f9fb fill, 1px #8998e6 border, #3d52b8 text, 36px tall, 0 18px padding, 9999px radius) and a "Sign up" #576ddb pill with #ffffff text at the same size.

## Components

### Pill Button — Periwinkle (Primary)
**Role:** Single conversion action per view

This is the only filled button in the system. It has a #576ddb background, #ffffff text, no border and a 9999px radius. Padding is 0 28px and height is 48px, set in Object Sans at 16px, weight 500, with -0.32px tracking and 1.0 line height, and no shadow. The nav variant shrinks to 36px high with 0 18px padding at 14px/500. The flat fill on a tinted canvas is deliberate: the color alone signals clickability, so no shadow or gradient is needed.

### Pill Button — Lavender Outline (Secondary)
**Role:** Sales and lower-commitment paths

This is a quieter sibling of the primary pill. It has a #f9f9fb fill, #3d52b8 text, a 1px #8998e6 border and a 9999px radius. Padding is 0 18px and height is 36px, set in Object Sans at 14px, weight 500, with 1.0 line height and no shadow. It shares the pill silhouette with the primary button but swaps fill for outline, so "Contact sales" reads as a peer of "Sign up" without competing with it.

### Navigation Bar
**Role:** Top-level wayfinding and account entry

The bar is transparent and not sticky. It is 64px tall, positioned relative, and sits directly on the #f9f9fb hero band with no border or shadow. The Ember Coral wordmark sits left, followed by Object Sans 14px/400 #1f1f47 menu triggers with small chevrons. Each trigger is a 64px-tall hit zone with 0 12px padding and a 4px radius. On the right sit the "Log in" text link (14px/500, #3d3d5c), the secondary pill and the primary pill. The nav dissolves into the hero instead of sitting on top of it as a toolbar.

### Email Capture Pill Input
**Role:** Hero sign-up with embedded CTA

This is a floating capsule field. It has a #ffffff fill, #1f1f47 value text, a 1px #eaedf6 border and a 9999px radius. It measures 480px by 64px, with 20px vertical padding, 28px left padding and the right side reserved for an embedded 48px primary pill. It is set in Object Sans 16px/400 with the `--shadow-sm` indigo shadow. It is the only input on the page and the only element that combines a hairline with a shadow, which deliberately marks it as the hero's focal object.

### Hero Stat Row
**Role:** Social proof as numerals

The row holds three metrics separated by hairlines. Each metric is a #576ddb numeral in Object Sans 24px/500 with -0.48px tracking and 1.375 line height. Below it sits a #3d3d5c label in Helvetica Neue 16px/300. Columns are divided by 1px #eaedf6 vertical rules with 16px gutters on each side, and there is no card background. The numerals use the action blue instead of ink, so the figures read as the product's output rather than as decoration.

### Department Card
**Role:** Main content card per team

This is a hairline-framed card with a tinted corner. It has a #ffffff base washed toward one frosted tint (#c1c9f6, #f7d4d4 or #c1f6e0) from the top-left, a 1px #eaedf6 border, a 16px radius and 24px padding. Inside are a 40px icon chip, a title in Object Sans 28px/400 #1f1f47 with -1.12px tracking, body text in Helvetica Neue 16px/300 #3d3d5c, and a footer link in Object Sans 14px/500 #3d52b8 ending in ">". The cards scroll horizontally with a fifth card peeking out. Each card's color temperature marks its audience while the structure stays identical.

### Icon Chip
**Role:** Category glyph holder

This is a white circle with a colored halo. It has a #ffffff fill, a 9999px radius and a 40px diameter, with no border. A filled glyph sits inside in #576ddb, #f2545c or a green drawn from the mint family (decorative, not a system token). The shadow matches the hue: `--shadow-md` for lilac, `--shadow-md-2` for rose and `--shadow-md-3` for mint. The shadows are colored to the glyph, which is the one place where elevation itself carries a brand hue.

### Feature Illustration Tile
**Role:** Platform capability with diagram

This is a soft tile that pairs an illustration with a caption. It has a #f9f9fb fill, a 1px #eaedf6 border and a 16px radius. The caption is a title in Helvetica Neue 18px/500 #1f1f47 and body text in Helvetica Neue 16px/300 #3d3d5c, with 24px padding. Tiles sit three across with a 32px gap. The diagram-first composition turns abstract infrastructure into visible objects.

### Platform Chip
**Role:** Labels nodes inside diagrams

This is a small pill used as a node in illustrations. It has a #ffffff fill, #1f1f47 text, a 9999px radius and 6px 12px padding. It is set in Helvetica Neue 16px/400 with a leading platform logo, and carries the `--shadow-sm` shadow. The chips ("Web", "Apple", "Google") are connected by dotted #576ddb lines and borrow the action pill's silhouette for read-only labels. This is an intentional echo, so the diagrams feel built from the same parts as the UI.

### Get-Started Panel
**Role:** Full-width docs entry point

This is a wide raised panel. It has a #ffffff fill, a 1px #eaedf6 border, a 16px radius, 48px internal padding and the `--shadow-lg` double violet shadow. The left column holds a heading in Object Sans 32px/500 #1f1f47 with -0.64px tracking, body text in Helvetica Neue 16px/300 #3d3d5c and a "See the docs >" link in #3d52b8. The right column is a grid of SDK logos on #f9f9fb tiles. It is the heaviest shadow on the page and is deliberately spent on the developer conversion point.

### Case Study Callout
**Role:** Customer proof with numeral highlight

This is a square logo tile beside a sentence. The tile has a #ffffff fill and a 32px radius, which is the system outlier, with the `--shadow-subtle` plum shadow and a faint #f7d4d4 corner wash. The sentence beside it is set in Object Sans 30px/400 #1f1f47 with 1.5 line height and -1.2px tracking. One numeral ("6000+") is recolored #f2545c, followed by a #3d52b8 "Read case study >" link. The 32px radius is allowed because the tile mimics an app icon, and the coral numeral is coral used as punctuation rather than decoration.

### Customer Logo Strip
**Role:** Trust band under the hero

This is a flat row of muted wordmarks. Five customer logos (Notion, OpenAI, VSCO, Ladder, Runna) are rendered in desaturated #6c7693 tones on the #f9f9fb hero band, spaced evenly across 1280px. Small "+" markers at the top-right of each slot hint at hover detail. There are no cards, borders or shadows. The strip removes customer brand color entirely, so the indigo ramp keeps control of the page.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Pull every text color from the indigo ramp: #1f1f47 for headings, #3d3d5c for body and #6c7693 for captions. The dye is the brand before any accent appears.
- Track Object Sans at -0.04em from 28px upward (-1.12px at 28px, -2.24px at 56px, -2.4px at 60px). This compresses the geometric letterforms into dense, wordmark-like blocks.
- Fill primary actions with #576ddb in a 9999px pill at Object Sans 16px/500, using 0 28px padding and 48px height. One action color makes every CTA instantly scannable.
- Set paragraphs in Helvetica Neue 300 at 16px/1.5 in #3d3d5c. The light reading weight lets 500-weight headlines dominate without bold body copy competing.
- Tint every shadow toward violet, for example `0px 6px 16px 0px rgba(61, 75, 143, 0.15)` on floating fields. Lift stays inside the indigo family instead of dropping gray smudges.
- Hold containers at 16px radius and actions at 9999px. Two shapes divide the page cleanly into things you read and things you press.
- Ration #f2545c to the wordmark and at most one highlighted numeral per section. Coral is a seal, and its scarcity is what makes it legible.

### Don't
- Don't reach for a neutral gray such as #333333 (not a system token) for body copy. It drains the indigo dye that defines the system, and #3d3d5c as the reading color is non-negotiable.
- Don't fill a CTA with #f2545c because it is "the brand color". Two competing action hues split the signal that #576ddb was built to carry alone.
- Don't push headlines to weight 700. Object Sans 700 appears in only 6 elements at 24px, and display sizes at 500 with -0.04em tracking already carry all the authority needed.
- Don't use black-based shadows like rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2). On the #f9f9fb canvas a gray halo reads as dirt instead of lift.
- Don't square primary buttons down to 4px. The 4px radius belongs only to nav hit zones, and a 4px CTA reads as a form control rather than an invitation.
- Don't use #c1c9f6, #f7d4d4 or #c1f6e0 as solid panel fills or text colors. They are corner washes and halos, and at full strength they turn the page into a pastel dashboard.
- Never ship 56px headlines at 0px tracking. Object Sans spreads wide at default spacing and loses the compact block silhouette.

## Imagery

The site uses product UI reconstructions, not photography. The hero is a layered collage: a JSON webhook panel, a subscriber line chart showing "14,274 Subscribers / 549 Trials", and a paywall editor with a phone preview. Photography appears only inside that phone mockup, and its colors are mockup-internal. Every frame sits on #ffffff with a 1px #eaedf6 border and a 16px radius, lifted by violet shadows. Icons are filled, solid glyphs in #576ddb or #f2545c, centered in white 40px circles. SDK logos sit in a grid of #f9f9fb tiles. Gradients are soft frosted washes in #c1c9f6, #f7d4d4 and #c1f6e0 bleeding from card corners. They are decorative, not system tokens, and never sit behind text at full strength. The narrative is that the infrastructure is already built and here is the dashboard to prove it.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1280px container, with headline blocks narrowed to 896px and intro paragraphs to 672px, all centered. Sections are separated by a 96px default gap and alternate between the #f9f9fb Mist band (hero, logo strip, paywall section) and the #ffffff canvas. The hero is a two-column split: a 60px headline, lede, email capture and three-stat row on the left, and an overlapping UI collage on the right. Department cards run four across in a horizontal scroller with a fifth card peeking. Feature tiles run three across with a 32px gap, and the logo row runs five across. The nav is 64px, relative, and transparent over the hero, with the wordmark and menus on the left and the account actions on the right. The footer is set as Helvetica Neue 16px link columns on #ffffff (estimated). At 375px, drop the display headline to 32px (heading), stack all grids to one column and use a 64px section gap. Density: spacious.

## Indigo Neutral Discipline

The system's defining move is that no neutral is neutral. Text #1f1f47, body #3d3d5c, caption #6c7693, hairline #eaedf6, band #f9f9fb, and even the shadow rgba values all lean toward blue-violet. The dye therefore reaches the page before any accent does. The discipline breaks the instant a stock gray enters: a #333333 paragraph (not a system token), a black 20% drop shadow, or a gray-filled logo strip. Each one reads as a stain on dyed paper. To extend the palette, derive the new value from the ramp rather than from a gray scale. Interpolate between #1f1f47 and #f9f9fb for any new text or surface step, and mix any new shadow from rgba(61, 75, 143) at an opacity no higher than 0.15.

## Tracking Ladder

Object Sans runs on a single compression rule: -0.04em at every size from 28px to 80px, and -0.02em at 24px and 32px for subheads and panel titles. Most marketing sites hand-tune tracking per breakpoint. Here the ratio is fixed, so a 28px card title and a 60px hero share one silhouette, and only the size changes. Applying the -0.04em ratio to Helvetica Neue body copy breaks the rule, as does leaving an Object Sans headline at 0px, because both mix compressed and loose texture within one block. To add a new display size, multiply it by -0.04 for letter-spacing and use line-height 1.125. Below 24px, release the tracking to 0px, except for the 16px button label at -0.32px.

## Rationed Coral

#f2545c is the brand's oldest color and also its most restricted one. It appears in the wordmark, in one statistic per section ("6000+") and in one icon glyph, and that is the whole budget. The convention in brand-led SaaS is to make the logo color the button color. RevenueCat deliberately does not, and gives actions to #576ddb so that coral can work as a seal of identity. The rule breaks when coral fills a button, tints a whole card, or marks more than one number in a sentence. To extend it, use coral only for single-word or single-numeral emphasis, pair it with the #f7d4d4 rose wash when it needs a halo, and keep it out of interactive states.
